slides.text: Two strings that steer the compiler 🎛️
slides.say: React Compiler has two directives: special strings that say whether a function gets compiled.
Use memo opts a function into compilation. Use no memo opts it out. Put the directive first in the function body, or it's ignored.
At the top of a file, before any imports, a directive applies to every function in it. A function level directive overrides it.

slides.text: In annotation mode, only "use memo" functions compile. Elsewhere, directives override the compiler's choice.
slides.say: In annotation mode, only functions marked use memo are compiled. In the other modes, directives override what the compiler would decide.

slides.text: Use them sparingly. Treat "use no memo" as temporary: add a TODO, fix the cause, remove it.
slides.say: Use them sparingly. Use no memo should be temporary. Add a to do note, fix the real problem, then remove it.
